page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.6xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs and 24 physical cores utilizing the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The system is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU hardware accelerators, relying entirely on external network storage options. Network connectivity is supported by an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Performance benchmarks place the ecs.hfg6.6xlarge in the average or middle 50% tier across multiple workloads. In CPU-focused evaluations, the instance achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1438.39 and a multi-core score of 23015.19, alongside a Geekbench multi-core score of 9875.0. Memory bandwidth tests recorded 1282.13 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 109.43 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 48.03 GB/sec for large-block writes. For specialized tasks, the processor's AVX-512 vector extensions support cryptographic and integer operations, yielding a Passmark encryption score of 10664.23 and a static web serving throughput of 17.13 GB/sec.

From a resource density and cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent execution times without the performance degradation associated with shared-core environments. However, the lack of bundled local storage requires users to factor in the latency and cost of network-attached storage. The instance is suitable for workloads such as static web serving, database operations, software compilation, and moderate-scale language model inference, where its 22.14 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and 12.72 tokens per second in 7B LLM text generation can be fully utilized.
